findings.title: Success criterion 1 demands zero matches in files whose remaining literals are explicitly out of scope
findings.description: The criterion requires the grep to return "zero matches in the six swept files," and names `WorkflowNavigator.ts` and `types.ts` among them. But the Excluded section (lines 49) and TD-3 state that `SliceStatus.status`'s `'complete'` member must not be swept, and it lives precisely in those two files: `WorkflowNavigator.ts:312`, `:345`, `:588` are `slice.status === 'complete'` / `status: 'complete'` (the `SliceStatus` union), and `types.ts:269` contains the union's `'complete'` literal. As written, the criterion can only be satisfied by sweeping sites the design says are out of scope — or it will fail verification. Narrow the criterion (e.g., exclude `SliceStatus` comparison lines, or drop `WorkflowNavigator.ts` from the zero-match list and rely on the explicit "excluded unions untouched" criterion).

findings.title: WorkflowNavigator is listed as a 3-site sweep target, but all three sites are the excluded `SliceStatus` union
findings.description: The Included table claims `WorkflowNavigator.ts` has 3 `` `=== 'complete'` `` sites to sweep (repeated at lines 75 and 90). Direct inspection confirms the file contains exactly three bare status literals — lines 312, 345, 588 — and every one is a `SliceStatus.status` comparison/assignment, which TD-3 and the Excluded section explicitly rule out as a different union. The file therefore has **zero** in-scope sites (its `NormalizedStatus` comparisons already use `STATUS` since 241, e.g. line 577). Remove the file from the included sweep (or restate what, if anything, is actually swept), so step 4 doesn't instruct an implementer to conflate the two unions the design warns against.

findings.title: Claim that no test asserts these literals is false
findings.description: "grep confirms zero `.test.ts` files assert against these literals directly (tests exercise behavior through parsers/fixtures, not string comparison)" is incorrect. Numerous tests assert the literals directly, e.g. `packages/core/tests/introspection/taskFileParser.test.ts:48` (`expect(result.inferredStatus).toBe('in-progress')`), `statusNormalizer.test.ts:24`, `slicePlanParser.test.ts:69`, `WorkflowNavigator.test.ts:89`, and `packages/cli/tests/commands/list-derived-status.test.ts:109`. The *conclusion* still holds — `STATUS.X === 'x'` by construction, so no test changes are needed and the suite remains a valid regression guard — but the stated evidence must be corrected to the actual reason (identical runtime values), since a reviewer auditing the claim will find it plainly false.

findings.title: Verification grep filter cannot work as written
findings.description: The command uses `grep -roE` (no `-n`), whose output is `path:match`, yet filters with `grep -v 'introspection/types.ts:[3-6]:'` — a line-number pattern that never matches without `-n`. Consequently the `STATUS` definition literals in `types.ts:3-6` are not excluded as intended, making the "Before: ~75 / After: 4" walkthrough arithmetic (line 149) unachievable with the given command. Add `-n`, or filter on the file only (`grep -v 'introspection/types.ts'`) while keeping the separate out-of-scope-list criterion.

findings.title: Site counts in the Included table are approximate but presented as exact
findings.description: Verification against the sources shows drift from the tabulated figures: `statusNormalizer.ts` has 14 `STATUS_MAP` entries (14 value-side literals), not "13 of 16"; `ConsistencyChecker.ts` has ~30–31 single-quoted value literals, not 36; `types.ts` non-`STATUS` literals are 4 (line 44) + 1 (`SliceStatus`), not 5 of 8. The totals (~65 across 6 files) are directionally right and the mechanical ordering/TD-2/TD-3 rationale are sound, but marking estimates as exact "Site count" values invites false precision in the walkthrough counts. Label the column as approximate or re-derive it from the same grep used in Success Criteria.

findings.title: Maintenance architecture's "test coverage before and after" principle is satisfied only implicitly
findings.description: The parent architecture (project-documents/user/architecture/900-arch.maintenance-and-refactoring.md, Architectural Principles) requires refactoring slices to have "test coverage verifying preserved behavior before and after the change." The design relies on the existing suite plus a before/after literal count and a deliberate typo-compile check, which is a reasonable reading for a value-identical sweep — no action needed unless the reviewer wants the criterion phrased explicitly as the satisfying evidence.
